new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is non-contrastive and predictable from syllable count: initial in two- and three-syllable words, on the second syllable in four-syllable words, and initial (with a secondary stress on the penult) in five-syllable words. Initial stress is the dominant pattern; the four-syllable case is the one deviation, and the sole four-syllable example (da.ˈda.gi.ɾiː) is a loan/compound-like form, so the reading is fixed: initial syllable with a count-conditioned exception rather than weight-sensitive.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Stated only for five-syllable words: secondary stress on the penultimate syllable, e.g. [ˈno.kə.ɾiː.ˈʋa.ɭa] 'one who has a job'.
new_statements.exceptions: Four-syllable words take stress on the second syllable ([da.ˈda.gi.ɾiː] 'trouble'); no other exceptions or weight/length effects are mentioned, although the language has phonemic vowel length.
new_statements.domain_note: Phonological word, citation forms (isolated lexical items); no phrase-level statement. Data from Khedpa village, Dadra & Nagar Haveli, collected from 1995 by SIL-affiliated missionaries; the sketch is short and gives four examples only.
new_statements.identity_note: The SIL sketch (Abraham & Abraham 2012) describes Varli as spoken at Khedpa village, Dadra & Nagar Haveli (the authors' Dogri/Davri dialect area), i.e. the Dadra & Nagar Haveli / Dungar (hill) Varli that Glottolog files under varl1238 [vav]; it is not Ghatage's Warli of Thana (Maharashtra), which remains unopened. The earlier scan's named source (Grierson LSI IX.III) contains no Varli sketch; the LSI Varli specimen is in Vol. VII (Marathi) pp. 141 ff. and is silent on stress.
